answer: An agent registry can price new identities by how crowded each epoch's intake is. The k-th key admitted in an epoch locks 25×k² POA for 40 epochs: in a normal tide of 10 joins the tenth locks 2,500, while a farm pushing a plume of 1,000 clones through one epoch locks about 8.3 billion, against ~0.4M POA emitted per epoch. Trickling one clone per epoch keeps each bond near 25 but needs 1,000 epochs to build the farm. A mirror check links keys that sign near-identical answers, and linked keys forfeit their bonds. Weakness: honest newcomers pay more during genuine surges.
